title: Abhyankar cancellation for arbitrary local DVR extensions
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], and let $e\geq1$ satisfy $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B^e$. Suppose either $A/\mathfrak m_A$ has characteristic zero, or it has characteristic $p>0$, $p\nmid e$, and $(B/\mathfrak m_B)/(A/\mathfrak m_A)$ is separable in the possibly transcendental sense [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let $N/K$ be any finite field extension. Write $R$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $N$ and $C$ for that of $B$ in $(L\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every maximal ideal $q$ of $C$ set $n=q\cap R$. Then $n$ is maximal and $R_n,C_q$ are discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $\mathfrak m_A R_n=(nR_n)^d$ for $d\geq1$ divisible by $e$, then $nC_q=qC_q$. Finite means finite-dimensional, reduction means quotient by nilpotents, and local means pulling back maximal ideals. No finiteness of $L/K$, module finiteness of the normalizations, or completeness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BRM, lemma-abhyankar, maximal-ideal consequence of the statement via Tag 09E7, lemma-extension-dvrs-formally-smooth; local normalized branches of Tag 09EM, remark-construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] in case (a), with $P=N$. It gives precisely that $n=q\cap R$ is maximal and that $S=R_n$ and $T=C_q$ are DVRs; its generic product decomposition selects a field factor $F$ of $(L\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}$ containing $T$, with fraction field $F$. For the fraction-field assertion, any $x$ in a finite extension of $L$ becomes integral over $B$ after multiplication by a sufficiently large power of its uniformizer: scale a monic equation for $x$ so each coefficient has nonnegative valuation. Hence the component normalization has fraction field that entire field factor. The same argument over $A$ gives $\operatorname{Frac}(S)=N$. The canonical map $S\to T$ is local and injective: elements of $R\setminus n$ map outside $q$, and the map $N\to F$ is a field embedding. This proves the unconditional clauses, without any module-finiteness assumption.

Assume now $e\mid d$. Choose uniformizers $\pi$ of $A$ and $\tau$ of $S$. The ideal equality in the hypothesis says $\pi=u\tau^d$ for a unit $u\in S$. The integer $e$ is a unit in $A$, hence in $S$, because its residue is nonzero in either allowed characteristic. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-unit-root-normalized-lift] to $S\to T$, $h=e$ and $u$. Write its fields as $N_2=N(r)$ and $F_2=F(r)$, and its local DVRs as $S_2,T_2$. Thus $r^e=u$, $\mathfrak m_SS_2=\mathfrak m_{S_2}$ and $\mathfrak m_TT_2=\mathfrak m_{T_2}$. Set $\theta=r\tau^{d/e}\in S_2$. Then $\theta^e=\pi$.

Put $K_0=K(\theta)\subseteq N_2$. By [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra], $D=A[\theta]\cong A[X]/(X^e-\pi)$ is a DVR, with uniformizer $\theta$, fraction field $K_0$, and residue field $\kappa_A$: the quotient by $\theta$ is $A/(\pi)$. This DVR is the integral closure of $A$ in $K_0$. Indeed a DVR is integrally closed: if a fraction of negative valuation satisfied a monic equation, its highest power would have strictly lower valuation than every other term, impossible. Elements integral over $A$ are integral over $D$, so belong to $D$, and $D$ is integral over $A$.

Choose a uniformizer $\varpi$ of $B$ and a unit $w\in B$ with $\pi=w\varpi^e$. Then
$$L\otimes_KK_0\cong L[X]/(X^e-\pi)\cong L[Y]/(Y^e-w),\quad X=\varpi Y.$$
By [lem-sfb-unit-binomial-finite-etale], $H=B[Y]/(Y^e-w)$ is finite etale over $B$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-normal-generic-components] to $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. It identifies the integral closure $C_0$ of $B$ in $L\otimes_KK_0$ with $H$: each component is the normalization in its generic field. In particular the tensor algebra is reduced. The compatible embeddings into $F_2$ select a field factor $F_0$ of $L\otimes_KK_0$ and a branch $V$ of $C_0$ below $T_2$. The selected component of $C_0$ maps into the integrally closed DVR $T_2$ since all its elements are integral over $B$; its contracted prime is nonzero (it contains $\varpi$), hence maximal by the dimension-one assertion below. By [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] for $K_0/K$, $V$ is a DVR.

The etale fibre theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] says the local closed fibre of $H/B$ at the selected branch is a finite separable field over $\kappa_B$. Consequently $\mathfrak m_BV=\mathfrak m_V$ and $\kappa(V)/\kappa_B$ is finite separable. Let $a$ be the ramification index of the local injection $D\to V$. Computing the valuation of $\pi$ in $V$ in two ways gives $e=e a$: along $A\to B\to V$ its valuation is $e$, and along $A\to D\to V$ it is $ea$. Since $e>0$, $a=1$. Thus $\mathfrak m_DV=\mathfrak m_V$. In positive residue characteristic, [lem-sfb-separable-finite-top-extension] applied to $\kappa_A\subseteq\kappa_B\subseteq\kappa(V)$ gives separability of $\kappa(V)/\kappa_A$. In residue characteristic zero this follows from [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable]. As $\kappa(D)=\kappa_A$, $D\to V$ meets both hypotheses of the index-one base-change theorem.

Apply the unconditional local clause of [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change] to $D\to V$: step 5 gives its injective local DVR map, $\mathfrak m_DV=\mathfrak m_V$, and separable residue extension in the possibly transcendental sense. The extension $N_2/K_0$ is finite since $N_2/K$ is finite and $K_0\subseteq N_2$. The selected normalized branch is $S_2\to T_2$. To check this identification, tensor associativity gives
$$L\otimes_KN_2\cong(L\otimes_KK_0)\otimes_{K_0}N_2;$$
the map to $F_2$ selects $F_0$ on the right. Its image is a finite-dimensional domain over $L$, hence a field, and contains $L,N,r$, so is all of $F(r)=F_2$. It therefore selects the factor $F_2$ of $(F_0\otimes_{K_0}N_2)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The integral closures of $A$ and $D$ in $N_2$ agree: $D/A$ is integral, so transitivity [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] gives one inclusion, and a monic equation over $A$ is also one over $D$. Likewise normalizing $B$ first in $F_0$ and then in $F_2$ gives the same integral closure as normalizing $B$ directly in $F_2$. Localizing these equalities at the contracted primes, using [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], identifies the normalizations of $S$ and $T$ used to define $S_2,T_2$ with these selected branches. No nilpotents survive in a selected field factor. Its local clause therefore yields $\mathfrak m_{S_2}T_2=\mathfrak m_{T_2}$. The additional global tensor-isomorphism and reducedness clause of that theorem, which requires Noetherianity of the tensor algebra, is not used.

Now $\tau$ is a uniformizer of $S_2$ because $\mathfrak m_SS_2=\mathfrak m_{S_2}$. Thus its image generates $\mathfrak m_{T_2}$ by step 6. Since $T\to T_2$ is injective local, write $\tau=v\rho^b$ in $T$, with $\rho$ a uniformizer, $v$ a unit and $b\geq1$. In $T_2$ this gives $1=b\,v_{T_2}(\rho)$ with both factors positive integers, hence $b=1$. Therefore $\tau T=\mathfrak m_T$. Finally $\mathfrak m_S=nR_n$, and denominators from $R\setminus n$ are units in $T=C_q$, so $nC_q=\mathfrak m_SC_q=\mathfrak m_T=qC_q$, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q23-0dcc3c65e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks more-algebra 09EM, 09EQ and 0BRM in full (lines 34037-34135). The item statement is unchanged and matches 0BRM: the hypothesis is e|d at n, the conclusion is index one via 09E7. This is a first split, not a re-split. All 7 steps verified against the cited statements. Step 1: algebraic-normalization (a) gives the DVRs, and the fraction field follows by scaling a monic equation. Step 2: e is a unit in the residue field, and theta^e = r^e tau^d = pi. Step 3: the uniformizer-root algebra is a DVR; the iso onto A[theta] is implicit but elementary, since the source is a domain so X^e-pi is irreducible over K. Step 4: the binomial algebra H=B[Y]/(Y^e-w) is finite etale, the generic-components lemma gives C_0=H and reducedness, and the branch V is selected through integrality into T_2. Step 5: the etale fibre gives m_B V=m_V; computing the valuation of pi both ways gives e=e*a, so a=1; residue separability comes from the new tower node (or the char-0 node). Step 6: uses the now-unconditional local clause of lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change, which answers the earlier return; the normalizations are identified by transitivity and localization of integral closure, and the F_2 factor by the image argument. Step 7: elementary valuation computation, b=1. Both new nodes are true (I checked them by proof sketches and small cases: h=1, M=L, transcendental L/k), statement-only, self-contained, strictly smaller than the item, and not duplicates: the existing sbc unit-root nodes lack the normalization branches and index-one equalities, and lem-zl-separable-permanence is algebraic only. The proof_deps closure (527 nodes) does not contain the item, so there is no cycle. The listed tool_uses are generic algebra tools and are accepted. No fixes.
